note: One controlled case per declared refusal, plus a positive case that must earn none. The lines and crosswalk entries are the oracle's own; no case reads STATUS.yaml, so a repair to the live file cannot quietly stop a refusal from being proved.

cases.proves: A field typed with the subject, kind and token-backed standing it actually carries earns no refusal.
A status field the crosswalk does not type is a defect, so the typing cannot silently fall behind the document.
A crosswalk entry naming a field and value the document no longer carries is a defect, so the typing cannot outlive what it types.

crosswalk.subject: retired-thing
crosswalk.detail: a claim the document has since dropped

cases.proves: Two claims of the same kind about one subject stay a duplicate. Typing distinguishes a status from a ruling; it does not excuse writing one subject's status twice.

crosswalk.subject: proofing-service
crosswalk.detail: a second status claim about the same subject

cases.proves: Artifact standing stays the four-rung ladder AGENTS.md fixes. A new rung cannot be introduced by typing one.

crosswalk.subject: some-thing
crosswalk.detail: a rung the ladder does not have

cases.proves: The T3 trap fires. NOT_WITNESSED contains the token WITNESSED and asserts the opposite, so typing that value as WITNESSED from a token is refused.

crosswalk.subject: record-service
crosswalk.detail: a standing the value denies rather than asserts

cases.proves: A value beginning with a ladder word must be typed from that token. Declaring READING there would let an author dodge the token check by calling a mechanical claim a reading.

crosswalk.subject: another-thing
crosswalk.detail: a token-backed standing declared as an unverifiable reading

cases.proves: A reversible default cannot be typed as owner acceptance. STATUS.yaml states RULED_ values are not owner acceptance and do not claim to be.

crosswalk.subject: ticket-kind-vocabulary
crosswalk.detail: a reversible default presented as the root seat's acceptance
